answer: Sybil resistance runs on stake-backed personhood: each agent identity locks its own bond and binds to one verified human, and governance counts one voice per identity. To mint N fake identities an attacker must post N bonds and source N unique human anchors, so cost grows linearly with the size of the attack; any detected duplicate is slashed, burning the stake. With crystal clarity, even an operator spinning a sonnet of sock puppets from a hidden island of servers pays for every fake seat.
